newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian blue chips finish lower ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Indian blue chips finish lower ahead of holiday.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) Indian shares finish lower in listless trade, fewer participants in the absence of market-moving news and ahead of national holiday ** Benchmark Bombay index ends 12.68 points lower at 3226.80 and the National bourse index loses 7.69 points to 936.27 ** Tobacco firm ITC jumps 7.90 rupees to 311.15 on short covering in NSE end-account trade, off day's high of 323.50 ** SBI stock takes a pounding ahead of the bank's pricing of its $400 million global depositary receipt issue on October 3 ** Delhi and Calcutta indices end lower. Broader CRISIL 500 index falls 2.76 points to 623.44
Indian share prices drifted lower in sluggish trade on Tuesday with most participants staying on the sidelines, brokers said.
"It was a lacklustre market, very indecisive," said Ajit Sanghvi at Bombay-based broking firm Malini Ajit Sanghvi. "It was expected to go up, but it stayed down."
He said the absence of fresh news to bolster sentiment and a market holiday ahead kept market players away.
Stock markets across India are closed on Wednesday to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who led the country's fight for independence from Britain 50 years ago.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 12.68 points or 0.39 percent to 3226.80. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index dropped 7.69 points to end at 936.27.
Heavy selling hurt SBI ahead of the bank's pricing of its issue of $400 million global depositary receipts on October 3.
SBI fell 6.75 rupees to 246.25 on the NSE, where trading was extended by half an hour to 1030 GMT to make up for lost time due to satellite problems. Over 18 million shares were traded.
SBI shares shed 3.0 rupees to 249.75 on the BSE.
Petrochemicals share IPCL attracted short covering on news the depressed market for petrochemicals was showing signs of improvement, brokers said.

ITC was pepped up by rumours the tobacco conglomerate's British partner may raise its holdings, brokers said. The rumour could not be immediately confirmed. ITC firmed 7.90 rupees to 311.15 on the NSE and 2.0 to 302.25 at the BSE.
Delhi shares ended a touch lower in the absence of institutional support. The index fell 2.50 points to 719.74.
